turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
I'd like to offer a supervised rewrite.
A rewrite for what? You haven't shown me a thing, and I'm not having Owen redo work to admit something he didn't do.
We're not finished. I still don't know who decided the zero or on what basis.
Sorry. The rewrite would replace the zero and nothing goes on his record.
Then it stays off his record no matter what, and I want that in writing tonight. That still doesn't tell me why there's a zero at all.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

In our meeting you said that a supervised rewrite would replace Owen's zero and that nothing would go on his record. I still require the basis for the zero, who decided it, and why it was entered before anyone contacted me. I expect that commitment in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Fallback position. Your promise that a rewrite would replace the zero with nothing on his record met her demand about his record, but she did not accept the rewrite, and she still wants to know who decided the zero and on what basis. The fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and you weren't there yet because no evidence was heard. Her time had not run out.
What moved her: You committed that the rewrite mark would replace the zero and nothing would go on his record, which met the one thing she will never give up.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before showing any evidence, so to her it looked like a request to admit something with nothing to justify it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your evidence never came near that night because you never showed any. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked who decided the zero and why Owen found out on his phone, own the timing in one sentence, then show her one dated, checkable piece of Owen's own work before you mention the rewrite.
Can you give me more detailed feedback? Like a full page?
